text: Sapling of Light
5 abilities unlocked through story progress that let Dante intervene in battle. Check unlocked abilities and remaining uses.
The Sapling of Light unlocks through story progress from 6-44 onward, with more abilities and uses unlocked later. Check the menu for what is currently available.
Normally usable once per day after clearing 6-44, and twice per day after 8-30. Each individual ability is limited to once per day. Uses refresh at the daily reset.
A use is consumed when you win the battle. Losses, retries, and withdrawals normally return it, but exceeding 100 turns consumes the use without counting as a victory.
Some challenge content, including Refraction Railway, has its own per-run limits instead of the ordinary daily allowance. Follow the content's specific rules.

The ordinary daily allowance is shared across Sapling abilities, and each ability can be used only once per day. Content such as Refraction Railway has separate per-run limits; check the current ability menu and battle counter.
The use becomes final on victory, rather than immediately when the button is pressed.

Target Redirection and Interception
Changing an enemy skill's target to yourself in a Focused Encounter. Check both the original target and Speed.
Drag your skill to an enemy skill slot. If its attack already targets you, an attack skill can Clash even when your Speed is lower or tied.

Intercepting an attack aimed at another ally requires higher Speed than that enemy slot. Equal Speed is insufficient. If the condition is not met, targeting it with an attack leaves the enemy's target unchanged and both attacks are unopposed.
Redirection and Clashing are separate. Defense skills can also redirect, but ordinary Guard or Evade defends instead of creating an attack Clash. Some Unclashable attacks can still be redirected.
If multiple allies select the same slot, the last valid redirection takes precedence. Recheck arrows after all selections to ensure the attack has not returned to the ally you intended to protect.
Being able to intercept does not guarantee a Clash Win. Check Speed and Skill Power separately.
Skills with rules such as unchangeable targets can override normal redirection.
Intercepting a multi-target attack's main target does not necessarily remove its subtarget hits on other allies.
Ally B at Speed 5 protects A from an enemy at Speed 4
Before: enemy 4 → ally A3
Ally B5 assigns an attack to the enemy slot
After: ally B5 Clashes with enemy 4
An ordinary single-target attack with no redirection restriction. At Speed 4, B could not intercept for another ally. A can Clash at Speed 3 because the attack already targets A.
Skill Slot
An action slot used to choose 1 skill. It is separate from Sinner count, Coin count, and Attack Weight.
Choose 1 attack or defense skill per slot. An Identity with 2 slots can select separate actions. Multiple Coins in one skill do not mean multiple action slots.
Under ordinary slot-growth rules, 1 living, non-Staggered ally gains 1 slot as turns advance. Allies with fewer slots take priority; ties favor earlier deployment order.

The standard allied total cap is 12 in Normal Encounters, or the stage's maximum deployment count in Focused Encounters. Starting a Focused Encounter below capacity lets living, active allies gain slots up to that cap; they do not all start with the maximum.
Deployment order is the order in which Sinners were selected, not Speed-based action order. Check the encounter for enemy slot counts and special slot changes.
Smaller teams have fewer actions on the opening turns before slots grow. Fewer members are not automatically better.
Do not assume survivors can replace every dead ally's slots. Dead allies' slots still count toward the total slot cap.
Stagger or canceled actions can make the number of executed actions lower than the number of selected slots.
Deploy A, B, and C in a Focused Encounter with capacity 5
Turn 1: A1 + B1 + C1 = 3 slots
Turn 2: A2 + B1 + C1 = 4 slots
Turn 3: A2 + B2 + C1 = 5 slots, reaching the cap
Deployment order is A → B → C. Everyone is alive and not Staggered, with no special slot changes. Turn 4 also has 5 total slots; C does not gain another 1.
Defense Skill Offset
Pairing ordinary Guard or Evade skills so neither receives the attack needed to activate. It is not a contest of Power.
Ordinary Guard and Evade generally activate when the selected enemy slot attacks. If that slot is also a defense skill, no attack comes and neither ordinary defense activates.
To offset an enemy's ordinary Evade in a Focused Encounter, aim an ally's Guard or Evade at it. Redirecting a defense aimed at someone else also requires meeting the Speed condition.
An attack assigned afterward by another ally can change its target again. Once all selections are complete, check which slot the enemy defense actually faces.
Offset does not erase every effect on a skill. Combat Start effects still activate independently.
Ordinary Counter cannot be offset: it responds to the first attack actually received regardless of its selected target, so another ally's hit can still trigger it.
Do not assume Clashable Guard and Clashable Counter follow ordinary Guard/Evade rules. Read their descriptions.
Your defense also does not activate, so do not rely on its Shield or On Use effects.
Pair an enemy's ordinary Evade with an ally's ordinary Guard
Enemy ordinary Evade ⇄ allied ordinary Guard
Neither receives an attack from its selected slot
Neither ordinary defense activates
Assumes valid redirection with no later reassignment. This is not an attack Clash or an ordinary Counter. Combat Start effects are handled separately.
Reading Effect Descriptions
Separate when, who, what, and how much. Selecting a skill does not activate every effect.
Read the bracketed trigger, target, effect type, value, and applicable turn in order. Effects listed under a Coin number belong to that Coin.

Combat Start on a skill means immediately after selections are complete and START is pressed. It is not the same as entering an encounter or Turn Start. Check specific descriptions when localization or individual effects use different wording.
For ordinary attack skills, On Use occurs immediately before the Clash, or before the attack if unopposed. On Clash Win requires an actual Clash victory and does not trigger from an unopposed attack.
Before Attack occurs after the Clash, just before attacking. On Hit requires the attack to land and does not activate if Evaded. On Heads Hit and On Tails Hit also require the stated Coin face.
Do not infer the recipient from Inflict or Gain alone: read self, target, or ally. Do not include next-turn effects in this turn's Power or Speed calculations.
Do not confuse On Use effects with On Hit effects that a Clash Win can prevent.
An On Clash Win effect does not guarantee the subsequent attack will land.
This basic timeline does not determine every priority among simultaneous effects. Special Coins, defense skills, and individual mechanics need their own descriptions.
From START to a successful ordinary attack
START: Combat Start
Immediately before the Clash: On Use
Compare Power: Clash
Victory determined: On Clash Win
Immediately before attacking: Before Attack
Attack lands: On Hit
This shows an ordinary-Coin attack that wins and hits. A Clash Loss stops this path; an unopposed attack skips Clash and On Clash Win.
Targets and applicable turns
Read who receives an effect separately from when it becomes active.
For example, On Hit, inflict 1 Bind on the target next turn requires a hit, affects the attack target, and becomes active next turn. It does not lower Speed this turn.
Also read targets such as self gains or grant to allies. Check whether the effect changes Potency or Count and how duration or consumption works.
Next turn is separate from the trigger. The effect does not appear automatically next turn if its activation condition was not met.

Parts and Part Breaks
Focused Encounter enemies can have separate HP, Stagger Thresholds, and actions for each part. Attacking a part also affects main-body HP.
An enemy's parts have their own HP, thresholds, and skills. Staggering a part stops that part's actions.
An attack aimed at a part's slot damages both the part and the main body. Damage calculation uses that targeted part's resistances.
Depleting part HP breaks it. Physical resistances generally worsen afterward, but whether it stops acting, regenerates, or becomes stronger depends on the enemy.
Excisable parts cannot be selected while broken. A break does not always immediately stop actions, so check the enemy description.
Reducing a part to 0 HP does not necessarily defeat the main body. Watch both HP values.
Post-break actions and regeneration have exceptions.
An attack on a part reaches both part and body
The part selected as the target
The same attack reduces part HP and main-body HP
Use the targeted part's resistances
HP-bar lengths and decreases are schematic, not exact values, ratios, or damage allocations.
Part breaks and excisable parts
The state after a part loses all HP depends on the enemy.
At 0 part HP, the part becomes broken. In many cases its actions are canceled and its Attack Type resistances become Fatal.
An excisable part cannot be targeted while broken. Other enemies keep attacking, revive, or strengthen after a break; follow their individual descriptions.
A Part Broken message alone does not prove the entire enemy is disabled or defeated.
